title: Which one fails?
examObjective: Converting between output types and data types using DataWeave
basics: The CSV writer needs flat rows: an Array of Objects whose values are all simple. A nested order has to be flattened into one row per line before it can be written as CSV.
prompt: Every script writes `application/csv` from the payload `[{"id":"o1","lines":[{"sku":"x","q":2}]}]`. Three produce a CSV. **One fails.** Which one?

options:
%dw 2.0
output application/csv header=false
---
payload flatMap ((o) -> o.lines map { order: o.id, sku: $.sku })

%dw 2.0
output application/csv
---
payload map { order: $.id, lines: sizeOf($.lines) }

%dw 2.0
output application/csv
---
payload flatMap ((o) -> o.lines map { order: o.id, sku: $.sku, q: $.q })

solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/csv
---
payload flatMap ((o) -> o.lines map { order: o.id, sku: $.sku, q: $.q })

explanation.approach: Writing the payload as it is gives the CSV writer a cell whose value is an Array of Objects, which it cannot put in a cell. Flattening the lines, or summarising them into a single value, gives it rows it can write.

snippets.label: The one that fails
snippets.note: A nested value has no cell to go in.

snippets.label: Flattened
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/csv
---
payload flatMap ((o) -> o.lines map { order: o.id, sku: $.sku, q: $.q })
